subject: Astraly launch: temporary rate uplifts & routing questions
messages:
From: Marta Chen <marta.chen@astraly.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: launchops@astraly.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Astraly Friday launch — expected traffic model + uplift request

Hi Rishi / Kim,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick follow-up: our team confirmed an initial public launch on Friday 2025-05-16 with a 24h window of heavy ingestion. Attached is our traffic model (summary inside). High level:
- Peak QPS estimate: 1,200 sustained for ~3 hours (30-min spikes to ~2,400)
- Total requests over 24h: ~200k calls (mix: 70% standard text-gen, 20% chat/structured, 10% embeddings for search)
- Typical request size: 80–350 tokens output

We need a temporary rate uplift for the launch window and guidance on routing to avoid hitting L2 throttles. Can Redwood support a short, time-bounded uplift + routing to dedicated endpoints? If so we need:
1) Numbers you recommend for a safe uplift (per-minute and concurrency)
2) Any product asks (warmup, caching flags, model variants) we should implement before Friday
3) Confirmation on SLA carveouts / escalation path if we hit throttles

I'll attach the detailed spreadsheet. Please advise who else you need from Redwood to answer the product/infra questions.

Appreciate the help — Marta

Attachments: Astraly_MAAP_traffic_model.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Marta Chen <marta.chen@astraly.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Astraly Friday launch — expected traffic model + uplift request

Marta — thanks for the model and context. Looping in Kim, Grace (CS/ops) and David (product/runtime) to scope what we need to do on our side. Quick clarifying Qs so we can give concrete numbers by EOD:
- Is the 200k calls figure total API calls or total user interactions? (we ask because multiple tokens calls per user can change token load)
- Of the 10% embeddings — is that batch offline or on-demand per user request? Embedding traffic has different CPU/GPU implications than generation calls
- Do you expect a steady ramp to peak or a hard switch (cold start) at T0?

From the platform side: we generally support temporary uplifts via a time-bounded quota override and routing to a dedicated pool. Product questions for David: what minimum provisioning we should pre-create to avoid cold K/V cache misses?

If we can answer the points above, we can propose a uplift plan (per-minute, per-100s concurrency, warmup sequence) and an ops playbook.

Thanks — Rishi

Marta — good details. Based on the numbers and typical token sizes, initial proposed temporary uplift:
- Time window: 2025-05-16 00:00 — 2025-05-16 23:59 (UTC to be agreed)
- Per-minute QPS uplift target: +3,000 calls/minute (allows for 30-min spikes)
- Concurrency safety: reserve +1500 concurrent slots across two dedicated endpoints

Product/ops pre-reqs we need from Astraly:
- A 72-hour ramp test (small warmup ramp from Tue->Thu) so we can seed caches. If you can run a 10% traffic warmup for 24h that helps a lot.
- Confirm whether embeddings are run synchronously (affects provisioning)

I've attached an SLA exception template and a short ops checklist for signoff. If you sign the SLA carveout and confirm the warmup, we can pre-provision the pool and set the temporary quota override.

Next steps for Redwood (owner in parens):
- Provision dedicated pool & route policy (Rishi)
- Pre-create warmup scripts & prefix cache seed (David)
- Establish a standby on-call (Grace)

Attachments: SLA-exception-template.docx

Thanks — Kim

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Marta Chen <marta.chen@astraly.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 May 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Astraly Friday launch — temporary rate uplifts & routing questions

Thanks for looping me in. A few technical constraints and asks from the runtime team:
1) Routing: we can route to two dedicated endpoints (L1/L2). For heavy interactive traffic use L1 (higher throughput, standard model). For long tails/large-contexts, route to a quantized L2 variant. We'll need a routing policy (simple header flag or per-route in the SDK).
2) Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for the 24h window. To meaningfully reduce tokens we need cache seeding during the warmup (Kim's 72h ramp).
3) Warmup requirements: pre-create 4 worker groups (each with 4 GPUs) and run the provided warmup script for 6 hours before T0. That avoids large KV cache cold misses and keeps latency under the SLO for the peak window.
4) Fallback: if throughput exceeds provisioned capacity we can failover to a smaller quantized model with graceful degradation; we need Astraly signoff because outputs can differ slightly.

Action items for Astraly:
- Confirm embedding behavior (sync vs batch) — affects memory sizing
- Approve routing header approach or provide SDK-level flag we can detect

I'm opening a short Jira for infrastructure work: https://jira.redwood/SERV-4279 (pre-provision pool + warmup automation). Please ack and we'll schedule a provisioning slot.

-David

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Marta Chen <marta.chen@astraly.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, launchops@astraly.com
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Astraly Friday launch — temporary rate uplifts & routing questions

Marta / team — summarizing next steps and owners so we can get signoff by Tue close: 

Redwood commitments (if Astraly signs SLA carveout & confirms warmup):
- Provisioning: pre-create 4 worker groups (4 GPUs each) and two dedicated endpoints (Rishi – provisioning OK to schedule on Mon 2025-05-12)
- Quota override: time-bounded +3,000 calls/minute for 2025-05-16 00:00-23:59 UTC, with automatic rollback at window end (Kim)
- Warmup automation: run warmup script 6h before T0 and seed KV cache during Tue-Thu 72h ramp (David)
- On-call: Grace will be standby during the window with escalation to Rishi and Product on-call

Astraly asks / confirmations needed (please reply):
1) Confirm embeddings are synchronous (yes/no) and % that will hit during peak
2) Sign the SLA-exception template attached (SLA-exception-template.docx)
3) Confirm whether you can run the 72h 10% warmup starting 2025-05-13
4) Signoff on the routing approach (header-based flag to route to L2 for long-contexts)

If we get affirmative on the four items today/Tue morning we will lock provisioning and quota override. If not, we may need to reduce the uplift window or provision additional buffer which requires finance approval.

Please reply with short "ACK" + item confirmations and we'll turn the Jira and provisioning into execution.

Thanks everyone — Rishi
